verdictHint.no_data: Collection failed; we could not read the data. It does NOT mean the service is absent.
verdictHint.unknown: Non-versioned tag; identical strings do not imply the same image.
verdictHint.conflict: One image name matched multiple workloads with different versions; refusing to judge.

recon.title: Version Comparison
recon.columns: Columns to compare (any combination; not limited to same-env pairs)
recon.pickHint: Tick the columns you want to compare, then hit Compare. Matching versions are green, mismatches red.
recon.empty: No data yet — configure environments on an platform, then collect.
recon.incomplete: These columns failed to collect and are marked no-data; this result is incomplete: {{cols}}
recon.planSaveHint: Saves the column set and ignore rules, not this run's results — results change on every refresh
recon.planDeleteHint: The column set will have to be picked again; existing results are unaffected
recon.needTwoColumns: Select at least two columns to export
recon.serviceHelp: By service name (last segment of the image name); wallet-* / *-backend / *api* supported. Comma or space separated. Empty = all
recon.mostlyMissing: Almost every row in this run is judged "missing" — usually that means the wrong columns were selected (two unrelated platforms put side by side), not that neither side deployed anything. Check which columns you picked.
recon.noMatch: No row matches the current filter — all {{total}} rows are filtered out; clear the filter to see them
recon.staleCols: These columns failed to refresh and are showing previously collected data: {{cols}}
recon.startReason: {{n}} column(s) selected. Click Compare to pull the latest versions and line them up - at least two columns are needed.
recon.excludedHint: {{n}} services in this column are filtered out by the collection rules (workload excludes / namespace scope) and take no part in the comparison. When the two sides use different rules you will see rows where one side has a version and the other reads “ignored” — that is not a match, it means we never collected this side.
recon.worstOverlap: "{{col}}" is what turns {{pct}}% of the rows into "missing" - its service scope differs greatly from the other columns. Try unchecking it.
recon.pickColumnsFirst: Pick the columns to compare, then hit Compare. Nothing is pre-selected on purpose - only you know which columns matter.

org.title: Platforms
org.hint: Our own side is just another platform, not a special case
org.empty: No platforms yet. Click Add platform to start.
org.name: Name
org.harborHint: Harbor host and project may differ per platform; the compare key is the last image-name segment.
org.credKeep: Credential set — leave blank to keep it
org.insecureTls: Skip TLS verification (only for self-signed certs)
org.compareHint: Unchecked = collect but do not judge (required for DEV/TEST: different Harbor and pipeline, build numbers not comparable)
org.clustersPh: One per line. Kite: cluster name; Rancher: clusterId (c-m-xxxx)
org.nsIncludePh: One per line, prefix like prod-* supported. Blank = all namespaces (needs cluster-level read)
org.nsExcludePh: Takes precedence over include. prod-* also matches prod-canary; exclude it here
org.overrideHint: Empty = inherit from platform. Fill in per environment when a customer runs two Ranchers (one for UAT, one for PROD)
org.saveFirst: Save the platform first — fetching clusters uses the stored credential
org.noClusters: No clusters returned — the account may lack permission, or this env has no endpoint yet
org.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}"? Its version snapshots and change history will no longer be visible.
org.wlIncludePh: One per line; wallet-* / *-backend / *api* supported. Empty = all in those namespaces
org.envCredRequired: ⚠️ An endpoint here requires its own credential — the override is all-or-nothing; endpoint alone leaves the credential empty and collection will fail auth
org.envCredInherit: Empty = inherit the platform-level endpoint and credential. If this environment has its own Kite/Rancher, fill in all three here
org.argocdScopeHint: ArgoCD only sees applications it manages. Services deployed manually or by other pipelines will not appear here. Leave cluster blank to match all destinations.
org.nsScopeHint: Read-only accounts are often project/namespace scoped (common with Rancher). Such accounts cannot list across all namespaces — list the ones you need here instead of widening permissions
org.enabledHint: Disabled platforms are excluded from comparison and collection; the config is kept
org.dsHint: Reference a configured datasource so you do not re-enter endpoint and credentials here.
org.dsUsing: Endpoint and credentials come from datasource “{{name}}” ({{endpoint}}). Edit it on the Datasources page.
org.noEnvYet: No environment yet - this project will not appear in comparisons until you add one
org.rulesCheckHint: Matches on workload names (same rule the collector uses); the sample includes services already excluded
org.rulesNoData: This environment has never been collected, cannot preview
org.rulesZero: 0 matches - this rule is new, is it spelled correctly?
org.rulesNeedRecollect: Saved. Service / namespace rules apply at collection time — run Collect again for them to take effect
org.rulesZeroActive: Saved but currently matches nothing - the environment may have changed, or it was wrong from the start
org.rulesKeptNote: Note: the sample is a filtered snapshot; this count excludes services already removed by active rules
org.envDsHint: When a customer runs separate Rancher instances for UAT and PROD, create one data source each and pick them here — credentials live in one place, so a password change does not have to be repeated per environment.

user.title: Users
user.hint: Role decides what you can do; visible platforms decide whose data you can see.
user.kickHint: Changing a role revokes that user's sessions immediately.
user.visiblePh: Blank = all; otherwise platform ids, comma-separated
user.deleteHint: The account and its sessions are removed; any active session is invalidated immediately
user.lockHint: While locked, {{user}} keeps the current role ({{role}}) on every SSO login instead of being remapped from IdP groups.
user.unlockHint: After unlocking, {{user}} role will be remapped from IdP groups on the next SSO login.
user.lockDaysHint: 365 max. Reverts to group mapping when it expires - a permanent lock would drift from the IdP forever.
user.lockReasonHint: Required. This is what you read when the lock comes up for review.
user.lockExpiringTitle: {{n}} role lock(s) expired or expiring soon - their roles revert to IdP group mapping
user.renewHint: {{user}}'s role is locked (currently {{role}}). Renew restarts the clock; Unlock lets IdP groups decide the role from the next SSO login.

token.title: MCP Tokens
token.hint: Read-only channel for AI. One token per client, each bound to a role.
token.onceOnly: The plaintext is shown only once. Copy it now.
token.name: Name
token.namePh: Client name, e.g. Ops AI Assistant
token.revokeConfirm: Revoke "{{name}}"? Any AI client using it stops working immediately and cannot be restored.
token.minPerm: Defaults to least privilege (read-only). Tools without permission are omitted from tools/list — listing then refusing makes the AI retry and treat an authorization limit as a fault.
token.usage: Usage: POST /api/mcp with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Tools: list_platforms / list_versions / compare_versions / get_service_version / list_changes
token.copyFailed: Copy failed (clipboard access denied) — select and copy manually; the token cannot be retrieved once this closes
token.daysHint: 365 max, counted from now. These are long-lived credentials handed to external parties and AI - an expiry date is what makes someone revisit whether it should still exist.
token.expiryHint: Set an expiry for token {{name}}. Once expired the API rejects it automatically.

sync.title: Source Harbor
sync.hint: The side we push images from. Sync records are what tell "their version differs" apart from "we never pushed it"
sync.deleteHint: Its policies and executions stop updating; existing records are kept
sync.name: Name
sync.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep unchanged. Passwords are never echoed back
sync.insecureHint: Only for internal Harbors with self-signed certs. Never for public endpoints
sync.emptyHint: Once configured you can see replication policies, per-run results, and attribute a version gap to "never pushed" vs "pushed but not deployed"
sync.policiesHint: Each rule pushes images to one platform. Pick the receiving side here (not ourselves) - only then can the comparison show sync status for that column
sync.noPoliciesHint: Click "Pull now", or confirm the Harbor really has replication policies
sync.execHint: Result of each replication run. A non-zero failure count means some image did not make it
sync.noExecHint: These policies have not run, or were just configured
sync.settingsHint: Source Harbors, replication policies, notification channels — set once
sync.guideTitle: Three steps to set up image sync
sync.guide1: Add a source Harbor — the side we push images from
sync.guide2: Click Pull now to import replication rules, then pick the receiving platform for each
sync.guide3: Add a notification channel, otherwise a failed sync goes unnoticed
sync.emptyCompact: No source Harbor yet. Follow the three steps above and connection status shows here
sync.policyFilterPh: One name per line; push-to-* / *-prod / *backup* supported. Empty = pull all
sync.policyFilterHint: A Harbor may hold dozens of policies while only a few matter here. Each policy costs 20 execution fetches per round — not filtering will slow Harbor down
sync.noTag: Harbor did not record a version
sync.noTagHint: When replicating by repository, Harbor only writes "repo [N item(s) in total]" without a concrete tag. So we can confirm the service was pushed, but not which version — the comparison shows these as "sync status unknown" rather than "not synced".
sync.hookHint: Polling the Harbor API cannot tell which version was pushed — it only writes "repo [N item(s) in total]" for multi-image replications. Webhook events carry the full version, and the sync attribution in the comparison depends on it. Create one under Harbor → Project → Webhooks with event type "Replication status changed".
sync.hookUrlLabel: Target URL (paste into the Harbor webhook)
sync.hookUrlNote: When ops-version and Harbor share a cluster and namespace, the service address is enough. Note: webhooks are per-project — every Harbor project with replication rules needs its own, or its events never arrive.
sync.hookTokenOnce: Shown only once — copy it into the Harbor Auth Header now. Only a hash is stored; not even we can retrieve it.
sync.hookNamePlaceholder: What it is for, e.g. "Harbor replication events"
sync.hookNone: No tokens yet. Requests without one are rejected — this endpoint writes comparison evidence, so no auth would let anyone fake a "synced" result.

notify.title: Notification channels
notify.hint: Failures always notify; manual success notifies; automatic success is recorded only (so failures do not drown in noise)
notify.name: Name
notify.deleteHint: It stops receiving notifications; existing delivery records are kept
notify.webhookKeep: Leave empty to keep unchanged. The webhook is a credential and is never echoed back
notify.webhookHint: Lark group bot webhook. Treat it as a credential — anyone holding it can post to the group
notify.emptyHint: Without one, a failed sync goes unnoticed — a "no channel configured" failed delivery is recorded instead
notify.recordsHint: Includes "skipped by rule" — so "why was I not notified" has an answer here
notify.noRecordsHint: A notification decision is made when an execution changes state

imgcheck.title: Check by service
imgcheck.hint: Pick a replication rule, then services - see whether each version made it across
imgcheck.inferenceWarning: ⚠️ This is inference, not a direct check: we have no account on the destination Harbor, so it combines "we have this version" with "a successful replication task exists". Purged replication records make a pushed version look unsynced; a manually deleted image on their side does the opposite. It answers "did we do our part" — which is also the only half we can fix
imgcheck.needProject: Select a Harbor and project first
imgcheck.noServices: No task details pulled yet - click Pull now above. If it stays empty after pulling, the details most likely failed to load (check server log for harborsync/tasks_failed) - this does NOT mean nothing was pushed
imgcheck.noTasks: No push records for the selected services - they may not be covered by any replication rule
imgcheck.deepLoading: Fetching all versions of {{svc}} from our Harbor…
imgcheck.deepTitle: Versions of {{svc}} in our Harbor ({{repo}}) - checked one by one
imgcheck.deepCapped: Showing only the latest {{n}} versions - earlier ones are not listed; do not assume they were all pushed

sso.title: Single Sign-On
sso.subtitle: Connect an identity provider and map its groups to roles
sso.displayNameHint: Shown on the login page button
sso.userinfoHint: Required. Group claims are often only returned by userinfo, not the id_token
sso.groupsClaimHint: groups is usually the org structure; app_roles is the application role. Getting this wrong means nobody matches
sso.allowUnmappedHint: When off, users matching no group are rejected instead of getting the default role
sso.mappingsHint: When several match, the highest role wins
sso.groupValueHint: Supports * wildcard, case-insensitive. Use * for all users
sso.noMappingHint: Without mappings, everyone signing in via SSO gets the default role
